note: THE TWO DEGENERATE INPUTS, and one of them is a gift. Emacs answers ((nil nil) (1 2)). For NO members it returns a regexp that matches NOTHING AT ALL -- its text is "\\(?:\\`a\\`\\)", an anchored `a' between the two ends of the subject, which no subject can satisfy -- rather than the empty regexp, which would match everywhere. kg can spell that inner form exactly: `\\`' and `\\'' have been kg's since 26.2 and frontier-regexp-shy-group-unsupported next door is the only part of Emacs' text kg cannot compile. For ONE member it returns the quoted member BARE, with no group around it, so a caller that concatenates gets what it deserves and s.el, which does not concatenate, gets the cheapest possible regexp. kg answers `void-function' at this pin. THIS CASE FLIPPED in the frontier demand phase, and the empty-member answer is Emacs' text MINUS its wrapper: kg emits `\\`a\\`', the inside of Emacs' `\\(?:\\`a\\`\\)', which no subject can satisfy -- proved against this case rather than argued, including against a subject that is the regexp's own text. A single member comes back bare, which is what mapconcat over one element gives for free.
